paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: no word from God will ever fail (Luke 1:37). Gabriel gives Mary the biggest news anyone has ever been handed, that her son will be called the Son of the Most High and that His kingdom will never end (Luke 1:32-33). And when she asks how, she gets a real answer, not a lecture. I think God can handle honest questions, and that's good news for a baker like you.

Now look at what Mary does with all that. She doesn't have the whole plan, and she has no idea how the next nine months are going to go. But she says, "I am the Lord's servant… May it happen to me according to your word." (Luke 1:38) I have changed my mind about a lot of things in my life, but this much I've learned: you don't need the whole map to say yes to the One who wrote it.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery today. When God says something, it stands, even when it sounds impossible, even when you're still wondering how. Elizabeth's old-age miracle was right there as proof (Luke 1:36), and Mary got to lean on it. What has God already said that you can lean on? Hold onto it, baker, because this story is just getting warmed up.
